body:
WHAT
The protocol package defines the two message families that cross the process boundary: `CoreEvent` (engine to frontend) and `FrontendRequest` (frontend to engine). `encodeFrame` turns a frame into one JSON line and `decodeFrames` turns lines back into objects, so any frame written on one side is read back identical on the other. A bad line becomes an error frame instead of an exception.

WHY
If a frame did not survive encoding, the app and engine would silently disagree about what was said, and a malformed line would tear down the session.

WHERE
engine/protocol/src/ndjson.ts — `encodeFrame()`, `decodeFrames()`, `parseLine()`; engine/protocol/src/types.ts — `type CoreEvent`, `type FrontendRequest`, `type Frame`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, supporting types `Usage`, `SessionSummary`, `RestoredMessage`, `ConnectionSpec`, `ImageAttachment`, `TaskItem`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. For a representative sample of every CoreEvent variant (session_started with commands/rateCard, turn_finished with usage, session_restored with toolCalls, permission_request, error, ...) decodeFrames(encodeFrame(ev)) yields a deep-equal object.
2. For every FrontendRequest variant (user_message with images, permission_response, set_connection with a nested vision block, question_response, install_addon, ...) the round trip is deep-equal.
3. Frames containing newlines, unicode (emoji, Turkish characters) and backslashes inside strings encode to exactly one line and decode back unchanged.
4. Concatenating the encoded output of N frames and decoding yields N frames in the same order.
5. Inserting a garbage line between two valid encoded frames yields [frame1, {type:'error', fatal:false,...}, frame2] with both good frames intact.
